paragraphs.title: Abijam's Reign and the Continuity of David's House

easy.explanation: Abijam reigned over Judah in the eighteenth year of king Jeroboam.
easy.q: Who reigned over Judah after Jeroboam's reign began?

easy.explanation: The KJV says, “Three years reigned he in Jerusalem.”
easy.q: How long did Abijam reign in Jerusalem?

easy.explanation: There was war between Abijam and Jeroboam.
easy.q: With whom was there war during Abijam's reign?

answers: His heart was not perfect with the Lord
He did that which was right in the eyes of the Lord
medium.explanation: Abijam walked in his father's sins, and his heart was not perfect with the Lord.

answers: Because of a league with Jeroboam
medium.explanation: For David's sake, the Lord gave Abijam “a lamp in Jerusalem, to set up his son after him.”
medium.q: Why did the Lord preserve a royal succession in Jerusalem despite Abijam's sins?

answers: A lamp used in the Temple
medium.explanation: The expression refers to preserving David's royal succession in Jerusalem.
medium.q: What does “a lamp in Jerusalem” mean in this passage?

answers: He sinned, yet David's royal house continued
He was king of Israel, yet lived in Jerusalem
He ended the war, yet lost the kingdom
challenge.explanation: Although Abijam was not fully devoted to the Lord, the royal line continued for David's sake.
challenge.q: What major contrast appears in the description of Abijam?

answers: The matter of Uriah the Hittite
challenge.explanation: David did not turn aside from the Lord's commands except in the matter of Uriah the Hittite.
challenge.q: What exception is mentioned in the account of David's obedience?

answers: Asa his son reigned in his stead
challenge.explanation: Abijam was buried in the city of David, and Asa his son reigned in his stead.

paragraphs.title: Asa: A King Who Follows the Lord

easy.explanation: Asa reigned in Jerusalem forty and one years.
easy.q: How long did Asa reign in Jerusalem?

answers: He did that which was right in the eyes of the Lord
He walked in the sins of Jeroboam
His heart was not perfect with the Lord
easy.explanation: The KJV says Asa did that which was right in the eyes of the Lord, as did David his father.
Asa removed Maachah his mother from being queen.
easy.q: Whom did Asa remove from being queen?

answers: He set it up in Jerusalem
medium.explanation: Asa destroyed her idol and burned it by the brook Kidron.
medium.q: What did Asa do to the idol Maachah had made?

medium.explanation: The idols were images associated with idolatrous worship.
medium.q: What does “idols” mean in this context?

answers: The treasures of the house of the Lord
medium.explanation: The high places were not removed, although Asa's heart was perfect with the Lord.
medium.q: What was not completely removed during Asa's reign?

answers: He did what was right, although the high places remained
He focused only on building cities
challenge.explanation: Asa followed the Lord and removed idols, but the high places were not removed.
challenge.q: How can Asa's leadership be described?

answers: He refused to interfere with his family
He put loyalty to the Lord above his mother's position
He gave the kingdom to Maachah
challenge.explanation: Asa removed his mother from being queen because of the idol she had made.
challenge.q: What does Asa's action concerning Maachah show?

answers: His father's dedicated things and his own dedicated things
challenge.explanation: He brought in silver, gold, and vessels that had been dedicated by his father and by himself.
challenge.q: What treasures did Asa bring into the house of the Lord?

paragraphs.title: The Conflict Between Asa and Baasha

easy.explanation: Baasha king of Israel built Ramah.
Asa sent silver and gold to Benhadad king of Syria.
easy.q: To whom did Asa appeal for help?

easy.explanation: Asa built Geba of Benjamin and Mizpah with the stones and timber from Ramah.
easy.q: Where did Asa use the materials taken from Ramah?

answers: To prevent people from going out or coming in to Asa
medium.explanation: Baasha built Ramah so that none might go out or come in to Asa king of Judah.

answers: To influence him to break his league with Baasha
To pay for building a wall
To collect a tax from Syria
medium.explanation: Asa sent silver and gold and asked Benhadad to break his league with Baasha.
medium.q: What was the purpose of the present Asa sent to Benhadad?

answers: He stopped building Ramah and dwelt in Tirzah
medium.explanation: When Baasha heard of the attack, he left off building Ramah and dwelt in Tirzah.
medium.q: What did Baasha do when he heard of Benhadad's attack?

answers: Asa took its stones and timber and used them to build other fortified places
challenge.explanation: The people carried away the stones and timber of Ramah, and Asa built Geba and Mizpah with them.
challenge.q: How did Ramah's building materials become a resource for Asa?

answers: Syria smote cities in northern Israel
challenge.explanation: Benhadad smote Ijon, Dan, Abelbethmaachah, Cinneroth, and the land of Naphtali.
challenge.q: What was the immediate result of Asa's appeal to Benhadad?

answers: Baasha built Ramah to restrict Judah, so Asa appealed to Benhadad for help
Asa's illness caused Ramah to be built
A war with the Philistines caused Baasha to rise
challenge.explanation: Baasha's fortification threatened Judah, leading Asa to seek help from Benhadad.

paragraphs.title: Nadab, Baasha's Revolt, and the Destruction of Jeroboam's House

easy.explanation: Nadab was Jeroboam's son and reigned over Israel.
Nadab reigned over Israel two years.
easy.q: How long did Nadab reign over Israel?

easy.explanation: Baasha conspired against Nadab and smote him at Gibbethon.

answers: In the way of his father Jeroboam and in his sin
medium.explanation: Nadab did evil and walked in the way of his father, in the sin by which Jeroboam made Israel sin.
medium.q: In whose way did Nadab walk?

answers: Surrounded the city in an attack
medium.explanation: To lay siege means to surround a city in preparation for capturing it.
medium.q: What does “laid siege to Gibbethon” mean?

answers: He destroyed all the house of Jeroboam
He restored Nadab to the throne
medium.explanation: Baasha left not to Jeroboam any that breathed, until he had destroyed him.
medium.q: What did Baasha do after he became king?

answers: Baasha destroyed all the house of Jeroboam
challenge.explanation: Baasha's destruction of Jeroboam's house fulfilled the word spoken by the Lord through Ahijah.
challenge.q: How was the prophecy of Ahijah the Shilonite fulfilled?

answers: His sins are given as the reason for the destruction of his house
challenge.explanation: The passage points to Jeroboam's sins and the sin he caused Israel to commit as the reason for judgment.
challenge.q: What connection is made between Jeroboam's sins and his house's fate?

answers: Baasha killed Nadab and then destroyed Jeroboam's house
Jeroboam's house was destroyed before Nadab reigned
Nadab killed Baasha and then reigned in his place
challenge.explanation: Baasha first killed Nadab, and after reigning he destroyed the house of Jeroboam.
challenge.q: What can be concluded from the order of events?

paragraphs.title: Baasha's Reign and the War with Judah

easy.explanation: Baasha is identified as the son of Ahijah.
Baasha reigned over Israel twenty and four years.
easy.q: How long did Baasha reign over Israel?

easy.explanation: Baasha reigned over Israel in Tirzah.

medium.explanation: The passage says there was war between Asa and Baasha all their days.
medium.q: Between whom did war continue throughout their reigns?

answers: He ruled over the whole kingdom of Israel
He ruled over Judah and Israel together
medium.explanation: The phrase indicates that Baasha ruled the entire northern kingdom of Israel.
medium.q: What does “over all Israel” indicate about Baasha's rule?

answers: He did neither good nor evil
He did evil and walked in the way of Jeroboam
medium.explanation: Baasha did evil in the sight of the Lord and walked in Jeroboam's way.

answers: The length of a reign does not prove faithfulness to the Lord
Anyone who reigns long must be righteous
challenge.explanation: The passage gives the length of Baasha's reign separately from its negative spiritual evaluation.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from Baasha reigning twenty-four years while still being described as evil?

answers: He is described as king of Israel during the continuing war with Asa
He is described as ending the war
He became king only after Asa died
challenge.explanation: The preceding verse mentions the continuing war between Asa and Baasha, and the next verse describes Baasha's reign.
challenge.q: How is Baasha's reign connected with the subject of war?

answers: Baasha also walked in the way of Jeroboam and made Israel sin
Baasha also removed the high places
challenge.explanation: Both Nadab and Baasha continued Jeroboam's sinful pattern and caused Israel to sin.
challenge.q: Which detail about Baasha repeats a pattern seen in Nadab?
